claim: RORγt+ group 3 innate lymphoid cells (ILC3s) maintain intestinal homeostasis through secretion of type 3 cytokines such as interleukin (IL)−17 and IL-22.
source: RORγt+ group 3 innate lymphoid cells (ILC3s) maintain intestinal homeostasis through secretion of type 3 cytokines such as interleukin (IL)−17 and IL-22.
evidence: Supported by citations to Sonnenberg et al., 2012; Gronke et al., 2019; Hernández et al., 2015; Zheng et al., 2008; Gladiator et al., 2013; Satoh-Takayama et al., 2008; Zenewicz et al., 2008 in the full text.

claim: CCR6- ILC3s co-express T-bet allowing for the acquisition of type 1 effector functions.
source: However, CCR6- ILC3s additionally co-express T-bet allowing for the acquisition of type 1 effector functions.
evidence: Supported by citations in the introduction section.

claim: c-Maf is a crucial negative regulator of murine T-bet+ CCR6- ILC3s.
source: Here, we identify c-Maf as a crucial negative regulator of murine T-bet+ CCR6- ILC3s.
evidence: Supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript including flow cytometry and RNA-seq analysis.

claim: c-Maf-deficient CCR6- ILC3s exhibit a hyper type 1 differentiation status, characterized by overexpression of ILC1/NK cell-related genes and downregulation of type 3 signature genes.
source: Phenotypic and transcriptomic profiling of c-Maf-deficient CCR6- ILC3s revealed a hyper type 1 differentiation status, characterized by overexpression of ILC1/NK cell-related genes and downregulation of type 3 signature genes.
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq data and flow cytometry analysis presented in Figure 2.

claim: c-Maf directly restrains T-bet expression.
source: On the molecular level, c-Maf directly restrained T-bet expression.
evidence: Supported by luciferase reporter assays showing c-Maf binding to Tbx21 promoter (Figure 3).

claim: c-Maf expression is dependent on T-bet.
source: Conversely, c-Maf expression was dependent on T-bet and regulated by IL-1β, IL-18 and Notch signals.
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data showing reduced c-Maf in T-bet-deficient mice (Figure 3F).

claim: c-Maf expression is regulated by IL-1β, IL-18 and Notch signals.
source: Conversely, c-Maf expression was dependent on T-bet and regulated by IL-1β, IL-18 and Notch signals.
evidence: Supported by in vitro stimulation experiments and qPCR data (Figure 3G-J).

claim: c-Maf forms a negative feedback loop with T-bet to preserve the identity of CCR6- ILC3s.
source: Thus, we define c-Maf as a crucial cell-intrinsic brake in the type 1 effector acquisition which forms a negative feedback loop with T-bet to preserve the identity of CCR6- ILC3s.
evidence: Inferred from the combined data showing c-Maf represses T-bet while T-bet promotes c-Maf expression.

claim: In mice, ILC3s consist of two major subsets: CCR6+ ILC3s that include lymphoid tissue inducer (LTi) cells and CCR6- ILC3s.
source: In mice, ILC3s consist of two major subsets, CCR6+ ILC3s that include lymphoid tissue inducer (LTi) cells and CCR6- ILC3s that can differentiate to cells expressing type 1 effector molecules, such as IFN-γ and the natural cytotoxic receptor NKp46 (Sawa et al., 2010; Klose et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to Sawa et al., 2010; Klose et al., 2013.

claim: CCR6- ILC3s can differentiate to cells expressing type 1 effector molecules, such as IFN-γ and the natural cytotoxic receptor NKp46.
source: In mice, ILC3s consist of two major subsets, CCR6+ ILC3s that include lymphoid tissue inducer (LTi) cells and CCR6- ILC3s that can differentiate to cells expressing type 1 effector molecules, such as IFN-γ and the natural cytotoxic receptor NKp46 (Sawa et al., 2010; Klose et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to Sawa et al., 2010; Klose et al., 2013.

claim: Fetal LTi and adult LTi-like CCR6+ ILC3s are essential for lymphoid organ development.
source: Functionally, fetal LTi and adult LTi-like CCR6+ ILC3s are essential for lymphoid organ development (Sun et al., 2000; Eberl et al., 2004)
evidence: Supported by citations to Sun et al., 2000; Eberl et al., 2004.

claim: NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s are implicated in type 1 inflammatory immune responses and may have pathogenic functions during intestinal inflammation.
source: while NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s are implicated in type 1 inflammatory immune responses and thus may also have pathogenic functions during intestinal inflammation (Klose et al., 2013; Powell et al., 2012; Buonocore et al., 2010; Bernink et al., 2013; Vonarbourg et al., 2010; Rankin et al., 2016; Song et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to Klose et al., 2013; Powell et al., 2012; Buonocore et al., 2010; Bernink et al., 2013; Vonarbourg et al., 2010; Rankin et al., 2016; Song et al., 2015.

claim: RORγt is strictly required for the development of all ILC3s.
source: The transcription factor (TF) RORγt is strictly required for the development of all ILC3s, as mice deficient for RORγt lack all ILC3 subsets (Eberl et al., 2004; Sanos et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citations to Eberl et al., 2004; Sanos et al., 2009.

claim: Mice deficient for RORγt lack all ILC3 subsets.
source: The transcription factor (TF) RORγt is strictly required for the development of all ILC3s, as mice deficient for RORγt lack all ILC3 subsets (Eberl et al., 2004; Sanos et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citations to Eberl et al., 2004; Sanos et al., 2009.

claim: RORγt controls the functionality of ILC3s by regulating the production of effector cytokines, such as IL-17 and IL-22.
source: RORγt also controls the functionality of ILC3s by regulating the production of effector cytokines, such as IL-17 and IL-22 (Ivanov et al., 2006; Rutz et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to Ivanov et al., 2006; Rutz et al., 2013.

claim: CCR6- ILC3 co-express RORγt and T-bet.
source: Interestingly, CCR6- ILC3 co-express RORγt and the master regulator of type 1 immunity, T-bet.
evidence: Supported by established scientific knowledge and citations in the manuscript.

claim: T-bet is key to the differentiation of NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s.
source: T-bet is key to the differentiation of NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s, as those cells fail to develop in mice lacking the gene encoding T-bet, Tbx21 (Klose et al., 2013; Rankin et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to Klose et al., 2013; Rankin et al., 2013.

claim: NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s fail to develop in mice lacking the gene encoding T-bet, Tbx21.
source: T-bet is key to the differentiation of NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s, as those cells fail to develop in mice lacking the gene encoding T-bet, Tbx21 (Klose et al., 2013; Rankin et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to Klose et al., 2013; Rankin et al., 2013.

claim: An increasing T-bet gradient enables functional plasticity of NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s by instructing a type 1 effector program in ILC3s.
source: Importantly, T-bet not only contributes to NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3 development, but an increasing T-bet gradient enables functional plasticity of NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s by instructing a type 1 effector program in ILC3s (Klose et al., 2013; Sciumé et al., 2012; Klose et al., 2014; Cella et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to Klose et al., 2013; Sciumé et al., 2012; Klose et al., 2014; Cella et al., 2019.

claim: Tunable T-bet expression in NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s serves as a dynamic molecular switch from a type 3 to a type 1 phenotype.
source: Tunable T-bet expression in NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s serves as a dynamic molecular switch from a type 3 to a type 1 phenotype (Klose et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Klose et al., 2013.

claim: When T-bet expression reaches a sufficient level, it can act as a repressor of RORγt, resulting in a full conversion of ILC3s to ILC1-like cells.
source: Once T-bet expression reaches a sufficient level, it can also act as a repressor of RORγt, resulting eventually in a full conversion of ILC3s to ILC1-like cells (referred to as ILC3-to-1 plasticity) (Vonarbourg et al., 2010; Cella et al., 2019; Bernink et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to Vonarbourg et al., 2010; Cella et al., 2019; Bernink et al., 2015.

claim: The balance between RORγt versus T-bet expression dictates the fate and function of CCR6- ILC3s.
source: Thus, the balance between RORγt versus T-bet expression dictates the fate and function of CCR6- ILC3s (Fang and Zhu, 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Fang and Zhu, 2017.

claim: The molecular mechanisms controlling the dynamic and quantitative co-expression of RORγt and T-bet in CCR6- ILC3s are largely undefined.
source: Importantly, the molecular mechanisms controlling the dynamic and quantitative co-expression of RORγt and T-bet in CCR6- ILC3s are largely undefined.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Cues from the microbiota, IL-23, IL-7 and Notch signaling promote or restrain T-bet-dependent plasticity.
source: Several extrinsic signals were shown to promote or restrain T-bet-dependent plasticity, most prominently cues from the microbiota, IL-23, IL-7 and Notch signaling (Klose et al., 2013; Sanos et al., 2009; Rankin et al., 2013; Viant et al., 2016; Chea et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to Klose et al., 2013; Sanos et al., 2009; Rankin et al., 2013; Viant et al., 2016; Chea et al., 2016.

claim: Exposure to pro-inflammatory cytokines, such as IL-12, IL-15 and IL-18, supports transdifferentiation to an ILC1-like fate.
source: Moreover, exposure to pro-inflammatory cytokines, such as IL-12, IL-15 and IL-18, was reported to further support transdifferentiation to an ILC1-like fate (Vonarbourg et al., 2010; Bernink et al., 2015; Satoh-Takayama et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citations to Vonarbourg et al., 2010; Bernink et al., 2015; Satoh-Takayama et al., 2010.

claim: c-Maf is a central regulator of RORγt+ CD4+ T cells, including RORγt+ Foxp3+ Treg cells.
source: In the past, our group and others could identify the AP-1 TF c-Maf as a central regulator of RORγt+ CD4+ T cells, including RORγt+ Foxp3+ Treg cells (Neumann et al., 2019; Xu et al., 2018; Wheaton et al., 2017)
evidence: Supported by citations to Neumann et al., 2019; Xu et al., 2018; Wheaton et al., 2017.

claim: c-Maf is a central regulator of RORγt+ Th17 cells.
source: In the past, our group and others could identify the AP-1 TF c-Maf as a central regulator of RORγt+ CD4+ T cells, including RORγt+ Foxp3+ Treg cells (Neumann et al., 2019; Xu et al., 2018; Wheaton et al., 2017), RORγt+ Th17 cells (Ciofani et al., 2012; Aschenbrenner et al., 2018; Tanaka et al., 2014)
evidence: Supported by citations to Ciofani et al., 2012; Aschenbrenner et al., 2018; Tanaka et al., 2014.

claim: c-Maf is a central regulator of RORγt+ γδ T cells.
source: In the past, our group and others could identify the AP-1 TF c-Maf as a central regulator of RORγt+ CD4+ T cells, including RORγt+ Foxp3+ Treg cells (Neumann et al., 2019; Xu et al., 2018; Wheaton et al., 2017), RORγt+ Th17 cells (Ciofani et al., 2012; Aschenbrenner et al., 2018; Tanaka et al., 2014) and RORγt+ γδ T cells (Zuberbuehler et al., 2019), both in mouse and human.
evidence: Supported by citation to Zuberbuehler et al., 2019.

claim: c-Maf directly binds and regulates key genes of RORγt+ T cells, including IL-22 and RORγt itself.
source: Specifically, c-Maf was shown to directly bind and regulate key genes of RORγt+ T cells, including IL-22 and RORγt itself (Tanaka et al., 2014; Zuberbuehler et al., 2019; Rutz et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to Tanaka et al., 2014; Zuberbuehler et al., 2019; Rutz et al., 2011.

claim: A broad transcriptional network analysis identified c-Maf as an important regulator of the ILC3-ILC1 balance.
source: Recently, a broad transcriptional network analysis also identified c-Maf as an important regulator of the ILC3-ILC1 balance, although the precise underlying molecular mechanisms have remained unclear (Pokrovskii et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to Pokrovskii et al., 2019.

claim: ILC3s express higher levels of c-Maf when compared to ILC1s or ILC2s.
source: This analysis showed that ILC3s expressed higher levels of c-Maf when compared to ILC1s or ILC2s (Figure 1A, gating strategy see Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Among the ILC3 subsets, c-Maf is particularly highly expressed by NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s at levels comparable to RORγt+ CD4+ T cells.
source: Among the ILC3 subsets, c-Maf was particularly highly expressed by NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s at levels comparable to RORγt+ CD4+ T cells (Figure 1B).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: RorcCre Maffl/fl mice show decreased frequencies of ILC3s in the small intestinal lamina propria.
source: Phenotypic analysis of siLP ILCs revealed decreased frequencies of ILC3s in the absence of c-Maf, whereas frequencies and total numbers of ILC1s and ILC2s were increased in RorcCre Maffl/fl mice when compared to littermate controls (Figure 1C).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: RorcCre Maffl/fl mice show increased frequencies and total numbers of ILC1s and ILC2s in the small intestinal lamina propria.
source: Phenotypic analysis of siLP ILCs revealed decreased frequencies of ILC3s in the absence of c-Maf, whereas frequencies and total numbers of ILC1s and ILC2s were increased in RorcCre Maffl/fl mice when compared to littermate controls (Figure 1C).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: RorcCre Maffl/fl mice show a selective loss of NKp46- CCR6- ILC3s.
source: Among ILC3s, we detected a selective loss of NKp46- CCR6- ILC3s in RorcCre Maffl/fl mice, while total numbers of NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s and CCR6+ ILC3s were not significantly changed (Figure 1D).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: c-Maf-deficient NKp46+ and NKp46- CCR6- ILC3s show significant downregulation of RORγt protein levels.
source: Importantly, flow cytometric intracellular staining also revealed a significant downregulation of RORγt protein levels in c-Maf-deficient NKp46+ and NKp46- CCR6- ILC3s, which was not observed in CCR6+ ILC3s (Figure 1E).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: RORγt protein levels are not altered in c-Maf-deficient CCR6+ ILC3s.
source: Importantly, flow cytometric intracellular staining also revealed a significant downregulation of RORγt protein levels in c-Maf-deficient NKp46+ and NKp46- CCR6- ILC3s, which was not observed in CCR6+ ILC3s (Figure 1E).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: NKp46+ and NKp46- CCR6- ILC3s from RorcCre Maffl/fl mice exhibit significantly reduced frequencies of IL-17A and IL-22 producers after ex vivo restimulation.
source: In line with the decrease in RORγt expression, NKp46+ and NKp46- CCR6- ILC3s from RorcCre Maffl/fl mice exhibited significantly reduced frequencies of IL-17A and IL-22 producers after ex vivo restimulation as compared to control cells (Figure 1F and G).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1F and G.

claim: No differences in IL-17A and IL-22 production were detected in CCR6+ ILC3s from RorcCre Maffl/fl mice.
source: Again, no differences were detected in CCR6+ ILC3s, corroborating the selective role of c-Maf for the homeostasis and function of CCR6- ILC3s.
evidence: Inferred from the experimental data presented in Figure 1F and G.

claim: c-Maf does not act as a repressor of IL-22 production in ILC3s.
source: Notably, c-Maf did not act as a repressor of IL-22 production in ILC3s, as it was shown for Th17 cells (Rutz et al., 2011), indicating essential differences in c-Maf function between ILCs and T cells.
evidence: Inferred from comparison with published data on Th17 cells (Rutz et al., 2011) and the experimental data in this manuscript.

claim: c-Maf expression strongly correlates with T-bet expression in both NKp46+ and NKp46- CCR6- ILC3s.
source: Interestingly, c-Maf expression strongly correlated with T-bet expression in both NKp46+ and NKp46- CCR6- ILC3s (Figure 2A).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: c-Maf deficiency results in strong upregulation of T-bet and NKp46 expression in CCR6- ILC3s.
source: More importantly, c-Maf deficiency resulted in strong upregulation of T-bet and NKp46 expression, both on the population (frequencies) and at single cell level (gMFI), in CCR6- ILC3s (Figure 2B).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: c-Maf-deficient CCR6- ILC3s show increased frequencies of IFN-γ producing cells.
source: In accordance with the increase in T-bet expression, we also detected increased frequencies of IFN-γ producing cells within c-Maf-deficient CCR6- ILC3s as compared to c-Maf-competent control cells (Figure 2C).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Ki67 staining of c-Maf-deficient CCR6- ILC3s is not altered.
source: Of note, Ki67 staining of c-Maf-deficient CCR6- ILC3s was not altered, ruling out that proliferative differences facilitated the skewing towards a type 1 phenotype in the absence of c-Maf (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The expression of T-bet by CCR6- ILC3s is not altered when c-Maf is selectively deleted in T cells.
source: The expression of T-bet by CCR6- ILC3s was not altered when c-Maf was selectively deleted in T cells, excluding that T cell-dependent alterations affected the type 1 conversion of ILC3s in RorcCre Maffl/fl mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data from Cd4Cre Maffl/fl mice shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: c-Maf-deficient CD4+ CCR6- ILC3s show higher expression of T-bet and NKp46 compared to their c-Maf-expressing counterparts.
source: We detected higher expression of T-bet and NKp46 in cells lacking c-Maf as compared to their c-Maf-expressing counterparts, indicating that the type 1 deviation of c-Maf-deficient CCR6- ILC3s was a cell-intrinsic phenomenon (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Mixed bone marrow chimeras confirm the cell-intrinsic function of c-Maf in restraining T-bet expression.
source: Importantly, mixed bone marrow chimeras of wild-type and c-Maf-deficient cells confirmed the cell-intrinsic function of c-Maf in restraining T-bet expression (Figure 2D).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data from mixed bone marrow chimeras shown in Figure 2D.

claim: c-Maf has been shown to attenuate the differentiation of Th1 cells.
source: Notably, c-Maf has also been shown to attenuate the differentiation of Th1 cells by a yet-to-be-defined mechanism (Ho et al., 1998), suggesting a broader role of c-Maf in restraining type 1 immune effector cells.
evidence: Supported by citation to Ho et al., 1998.

claim: 941 genes are differentially expressed between c-Maf-deficient and control NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s.
source: We identified 941 genes as differentially expressed (FC > 1.5, p-value < 0.05) between c-Maf-deficient and control NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s (Figure 2E, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 2E and Supplementary file 1.

claim: Only ca. 30% of genes differentially expressed in NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s are also differentially expressed in CCR6+ ILC3s.
source: Interestingly, only ca. 30% of these genes (294 genes) were also found to be differentially expressed in CCR6+ ILC3s (Figure 2—figure supplement 2C, Supplementary file 2), indicating a distinct function of c-Maf in NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s.
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2C and Supplementary file 2.

claim: c-Maf-deficient NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s show a striking enrichment of type 1 and NK cell-related genes.
source: Consistent with our flow cytometry data, we detected a striking enrichment of type 1 and NK cell-related genes (e.g. Tbx21, Ifng, Nos2, Klri2, Klrc1, Klrc2, Gzmb, Gzmd, Fasl) in c-Maf-deficient NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s (Figure 2E).
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Bcl6 and Irf8 are significantly upregulated in the absence of c-Maf in NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s.
source: In line with this, Bcl6 and Irf8, both recently described as crucial transcription factors promoting ILC1/NK cell gene programs (Pokrovskii et al., 2019; Adams et al., 2018), were also significantly upregulated in the absence of c-Maf in NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s (Figure 2E, Figure 2—figure supplement 2D and E).
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 2E and Figure 2—figure supplement 2D and E, and citations to Pokrovskii et al., 2019; Adams et al., 2018.

claim: Several type 3 effector genes are downregulated in NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s upon c-Maf-deficiency.
source: Conversely, several type 3 effector genes (e.g. Il17a, Il17f, Il17re, Ccl20) were downregulated in NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s upon c-Maf-deficiency (Figure 2E).
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: ILC1 and NK cell gene signatures are significantly enriched in c-Maf-deficient NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s.
source: Importantly, when applied to GSEA, both gene signatures were significantly enriched in c-Maf-deficient NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s (Figure 2F), indicating a global shift in gene expression towards an ILC1/NK cell phenotype.
evidence: Supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 2F.

claim: NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s are largely considered to be non-toxic cells.
source: The latter finding is particularly interesting, since NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s are largely considered to be non-toxic cells (Melo-Gonzalez and Hepworth, 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Melo-Gonzalez and Hepworth, 2017.

claim: NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s share a considerable transcriptional overlap with ILC1s.
source: Nevertheless, NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s share a considerable transcriptional overlap with ILC1s, which also exhibit a degree of cytotoxic capacity (Robinette et al., 2015; Cortez and Colonna, 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to Robinette et al., 2015; Cortez and Colonna, 2016.

claim: ILC1s exhibit a degree of cytotoxic capacity.
source: Nevertheless, NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s share a considerable transcriptional overlap with ILC1s, which also exhibit a degree of cytotoxic capacity (Robinette et al., 2015; Cortez and Colonna, 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to Robinette et al., 2015; Cortez and Colonna, 2016.

claim: c-Maf-deficiency may result in marked cytotoxicity of NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s.
source: Thus, c-Maf-deficiency may result in marked cytotoxicity of NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the observed upregulation of cytotoxic genes.

claim: Maf response elements (MARE) are present within the Tbx21 promoter.
source: Indeed, in silico analysis identified Maf response elements (MARE) within the Tbx21 promoter, as well as in a conserved distant Tbx21 enhancer (Kataoka et al., 1994; Yang et al., 2007), both regions accessible in NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s as evidenced by ATAC-sequencing (Shih et al., 2016; Figure 3A and B).
evidence: Supported by in silico analysis and ATAC-seq data (Shih et al., 2016) shown in Figure 3A and B, and citations to Kataoka et al., 1994; Yang et al., 2007.

claim: Maf response elements (MARE) are present in a conserved distant Tbx21 enhancer.
source: Indeed, in silico analysis identified Maf response elements (MARE) within the Tbx21 promoter, as well as in a conserved distant Tbx21 enhancer (Kataoka et al., 1994; Yang et al., 2007), both regions accessible in NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s as evidenced by ATAC-sequencing (Shih et al., 2016; Figure 3A and B).
evidence: Supported by in silico analysis and ATAC-seq data (Shih et al., 2016) shown in Figure 3A and B, and citations to Kataoka et al., 1994; Yang et al., 2007.

claim: The Tbx21 promoter and enhancer regions are accessible in NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s.
source: Indeed, in silico analysis identified Maf response elements (MARE) within the Tbx21 promoter, as well as in a conserved distant Tbx21 enhancer (Kataoka et al., 1994; Yang et al., 2007), both regions accessible in NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s as evidenced by ATAC-sequencing (Shih et al., 2016; Figure 3A and B).
evidence: Supported by ATAC-seq data (Shih et al., 2016) shown in Figure 3A and B.

claim: The Tbx21 promoter shows strong transcriptional activity.
source: Indeed, the Tbx21 promoter showed strong transcriptional activity when compared to a promoterless control vector (Figure 3D).
evidence: Supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The Tbx21 enhancer increases transcriptional activity when cloned upstream of the Tbx21 promoter.
source: The Tbx21 enhancer further increased this activity when cloned upstream of the Tbx21 promoter (Figure 3D).
evidence: Supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Mutating the MARE sites within the Tbx21 promoter results in de-repression of reporter signal upon c-Maf overexpression.
source: Importantly, upon exogenous overexpression of c-Maf, we detected a strong de-repression of the reporter signal when we mutated the MARE sites within the Tbx21 promoter (Figure 3B and E).
evidence: Supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: c-Maf facilitates its suppressive function mainly by acting on the Tbx21 promoter.
source: Notably, mutating the Tbx21 enhancer did not result in further increase of reporter activity, indicating that c-Maf facilitated its suppressive function mainly by acting on the Tbx21 promoter (Figure 3B and E).
evidence: Inferred from luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: In the absence of T-bet, c-Maf expression is strongly reduced in CCR6- ILC3s.
source: Indeed, in the absence of T-bet, c-Maf expression was strongly reduced when compared to T-bet-sufficient cells (Figure 3F), indicating that T-bet positively regulated its own repressor to establish an equilibrated state within the ILC3-to-ILC1 continuum.
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data from T-bet-deficient mice shown in Figure 3F.

claim: T-bet positively regulates c-Maf to establish an equilibrated state within the ILC3-to-ILC1 continuum.
source: Indeed, in the absence of T-bet, c-Maf expression was strongly reduced when compared to T-bet-sufficient cells (Figure 3F), indicating that T-bet positively regulated its own repressor to establish an equilibrated state within the ILC3-to-ILC1 continuum.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that c-Maf expression is reduced in T-bet-deficient mice.

claim: T-bet binding peaks overlap with open chromatin regions in NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s within two conserved non-coding sequences upstream of Maf.
source: In silico analysis of the Maf locus using ATAC-Seq (Shih et al., 2016) and T-bet ChIP-Seq (Gökmen et al., 2013) data further identified a striking overlap of T-bet binding peaks with open chromatin regions in NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s within two conserved non-coding sequences (CNS-0.5 and CNS-1) upstream of Maf, suggesting that T-bet directly controlled c-Maf expression in CCR6- ILC3s (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by ATAC-seq (Shih et al., 2016) and T-bet ChIP-seq (Gökmen et al., 2013) data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: T-bet directly controls c-Maf expression in CCR6- ILC3s.
source: In silico analysis of the Maf locus using ATAC-Seq (Shih et al., 2016) and T-bet ChIP-Seq (Gökmen et al., 2013) data further identified a striking overlap of T-bet binding peaks with open chromatin regions in NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s within two conserved non-coding sequences (CNS-0.5 and CNS-1) upstream of Maf, suggesting that T-bet directly controlled c-Maf expression in CCR6- ILC3s (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Inferred from ATAC-seq and ChIP-seq data showing T-bet binding at Maf regulatory regions.

claim: IL-1β and IL-18 are potent inducers of Maf expression in NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s.
source: Among all tested conditions, the pro-inflammatory IL-1 family cytokines IL-1ß and IL-18 stood out as potent inducers of Maf expression (Figure 3G).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data from in vitro stimulation experiments shown in Figure 3G.

claim: IL-1β/IL-18 stimulation induces Ifng and Il22 expression in NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s.
source: IL-1ß/IL-18 stimulation also induced Ifng and Il22 expression (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: c-Maf-deficient NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s express more Ifng in response to IL-1β/IL-18 compared to controls.
source: In fact, c-Maf-deficient NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s expressed more Ifng in response to IL-1ß/IL-18 as compared to controls (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A), functionally connecting c-Maf expression downstream of these stimuli with the control of the type 1 effector response.
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: A conserved NF-κb binding site is present within CNS-0.5 upstream of Maf.
source: Since both IL-1ß and IL-18 signal via NF-κb and a conserved NF-κb binding site is present within CNS-0.5 upstream of Maf (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and D), we hypothesized that NF-κb is involved in regulation of c-Maf expression downstream of IL-1ß/IL-18.
evidence: Supported by in silico analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and D.

claim: Pharmacological inhibition of NF-κb signalling completely abrogates the IL-1β/IL-18-mediated induction of c-Maf expression.
source: Indeed, pharmacological inhibition of NF-κb signalling completely abrogated the cytokine-mediated induction of c-Maf expression (Figure 3H).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data from experiments using NF-κb inhibitor shown in Figure 3H.

claim: IL-12 suppresses Maf expression in NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s.
source: In addition to IL-1ß/IL-18, we found that IL-12 suppressed Maf expression (Figure 3G).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: IL-12 does not interfere with the IL-1β/IL-18-mediated c-Maf induction.
source: However, IL-12 did not interfere with the IL-1ß/IL-18-mediated c-Maf induction nor was c-Maf expression altered in NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s from Il12a-/- mice as compared to controls (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B and C), questioning a dominant role of IL-12 in c-Maf regulation.
evidence: Supported by qPCR and flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B and C.

claim: c-Maf expression is not altered in NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s from Il12a-/- mice.
source: However, IL-12 did not interfere with the IL-1ß/IL-18-mediated c-Maf induction nor was c-Maf expression altered in NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s from Il12a-/- mice as compared to controls (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B and C), questioning a dominant role of IL-12 in c-Maf regulation.
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2C.

claim: IL-1β/IL-18 stimulation is accompanied by a concomitant decrease in Tbx21 expression.
source: Of note, the cytokine-mediated induction of Maf expression was accompanied by a concomitant decrease in Tbx21 expression (Figure 3—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2D.

claim: The suppression of Tbx21 by IL-1β/IL-18 is independent of NF-κb and c-Maf.
source: Yet, this suppression was independent of NF-κb and c-Maf, since Tbx21 expression was similarly suppressed by IL-1ß/IL-18 upon NF-κb inhibiton and in c-Maf-deficient NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s (Figure 3—figure supplement 2E and F).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2E and F.

claim: Notch is necessary for the induction and maintenance of T-bet and NKp46 expression in CCR6- ILC3s.
source: Indeed, Notch was shown to be necessary for the induction and maintenance of T-bet and NKp46 expression in CCR6- ILC3s (Rankin et al., 2013; Viant et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to Rankin et al., 2013; Viant et al., 2016.

claim: Notch signals are essential to drive type 1 conversion of NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s.
source: As reported earlier, Notch signals were essential to drive type 1 conversion of NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s, as evidenced by reduction and loss of NKp46 expression in the absence of Notch (Figure 3I).
evidence: Supported by in vitro culture data on OP9 vs OP9-DLL1 cells shown in Figure 3I.

claim: c-Maf expression is significantly reduced in NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s cultured on OP9 cells compared to cells cultured on OP9-DLL1 cells.
source: Importantly, c-Maf showed a similar expression pattern, being significantly reduced in NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s cultured on OP9 cells as compared to cells cultured on OP9-DLL1 cells (Figure 3J).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data from OP9 vs OP9-DLL1 culture experiments shown in Figure 3J.

claim: The downregulation of NKp46 and c-Maf expression in the absence of continuous Notch signalling is independent of potential survival promoting effects of Notch.
source: This downregulation of NKp46 and c-Maf expression in the absence of continuous Notch signalling was independent of potential survival promoting effects of Notch (Figure 3—figure supplement 3), establishing a molecular link between Notch signalling and type 1 conversion of NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s.
evidence: Supported by proliferation analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: Co-expression and cross-regulation of multiple master regulators determines the fate and function of ILCs.
source: Collectively, our study adds c-Maf as a novel key factor to the complex transcriptional network that governs the differentiation and function of ILC3s. In line with the emerging concept that co-expression and cross-regulation of multiple master regulators determines the fate and function of ILCs (Fang and Zhu, 2017), we have uncovered an essential negative feedback loop between c-Maf and T-bet, which restrains the type 1 conversion of ILC3s.
evidence: Supported by citation to Fang and Zhu, 2017.

claim: The c-Maf-dependent suppression of T-bet indirectly stabilizes RORγt expression.
source: Given the antagonism between T-bet and RORγt, the c-Maf-dependent suppression of T-bet also indirectly stabilizes RORγt expression, thus preserving the type 3 identity of ILC3s.
evidence: Inferred from the known antagonism between T-bet and RORγt and the observed effects of c-Maf on T-bet.

claim: c-Maf may directly contribute to RORγt expression in ILC3s.
source: In addition, c-Maf may also directly contribute to RORγt expression in ILC3s, as it has been reported for T cells (Tanaka et al., 2014; Zuberbuehler et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on findings in T cells.

claim: Notch was identified as a potent inducer of c-Maf expression in T cells.
source: Similarly, we could recently identify Notch signalling as a potent inducer of c-Maf expression in T cells (Neumann et al., 2019; Neumann et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to Neumann et al., 2019; Neumann et al., 2014.

claim: Conditional deletion of c-Maf in T cells causes disturbances in intestinal homeostasis.
source: Moreover, conditional deletion of c-Maf in T cells (Cd4Cre Maffl/fl or Foxp3Cre Maffl/fl) was reported to cause disturbances in intestinal homeostasis (Neumann et al., 2019; Imbratta et al., 2019)
evidence: Supported by citations to Neumann et al., 2019; Imbratta et al., 2019.

claim: A small subset of CCR6- ILC3s co-expresses CD4 (ca. 2% of CCR6- ILC3s).
source: Interestingly, a small subset of CCR6- ILC3s also co-expresses CD4 (ca. 2% of CCR6- ILC3s, Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: c-Maf staining of CD4+ CCR6- ILC3s from Cd4Cre Maffl/fl mice confirms c-Maf deletion in a substantial fraction of cells (ca. 50%).
source: Indeed, c-Maf staining of CD4+ CCR6- ILC3s from Cd4Cre Maffl/fl mice confirmed c-Maf deletion in a substantial fraction of cells (ca. 50%), allowing us to compare c-Maf-competent and c-Maf-deficient CCR6- ILC3s within the same mouse (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: c-Maf-deficient ILC3s cluster separately from their wild-type counterparts in principal component analysis.
source: Principal component analysis showed that c-Maf-deficient ILC3s clustered separately from their wild-type counterparts, demonstrating a unique role of c-Maf in shaping the transcriptome of ILC3s (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: Supported by PCA analysis of RNA-seq data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2B.

claim: The function of c-Maf is specific to NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s as opposed to CCR6+ ILC3s.
source: In summary, these data demonstrated that c-Maf was essential to globally balance type 1 and type 3 gene programs within CCR6- ILC3s. This function of c-Maf was specific to NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s as opposed to CCR6+ ILC3s, most likely due to the particularly high c-Maf expression and the selective accessible of type 1 gene loci in these cells (Pokrovskii et al., 2019; Shih et al., 2016).
evidence: Inferred from the differential gene expression patterns and supported by citations to Pokrovskii et al., 2019; Shih et al., 2016.

claim: The particularly high c-Maf expression and the selective accessibility of type 1 gene loci in NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s likely explain the specific function of c-Maf in these cells.
source: This function of c-Maf was specific to NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s as opposed to CCR6+ ILC3s, most likely due to the particularly high c-Maf expression and the selective accessible of type 1 gene loci in these cells (Pokrovskii et al., 2019; Shih et al., 2016).
evidence: This is an inference based on observed expression patterns and chromatin accessibility data.

claim: In the absence of c-Maf, NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s downregulate type 3 effector genes while overexpressing numerous genes encoding for type 1 and cytotoxic effector molecules.
source: In the absence of c-Maf, NKp46+ CCR6- ILC3s downregulated type 3 effector genes, while overexpressing numerous genes encoding for type 1 and cytotoxic effector molecules.
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Bcl6 and Irf8 are crucial transcription factors promoting ILC1/NK cell gene programs.
source: In line with this, Bcl6 and Irf8, both recently described as crucial transcription factors promoting ILC1/NK cell gene programs (Pokrovskii et al., 2019; Adams et al., 2018)
evidence: Supported by citations to Pokrovskii et al., 2019; Adams et al., 2018.
